question: whystream
answer: My project asks what an LLM represents about the partner it is talking to, and whether that representation updates. The stream asks that of model internals. Qwen3.8-27B learns which frame a hidden partner responds to (gain 0.187). The effect survives a reworded prompt (0.207), fails on Gemma-4-31B (0.040), and vanishes when Qwen must state probabilities. There the choice equalled the argmax of the stated belief in 3,600 of 3,600 records. Behaviour alone cannot show a separable partner model. Activations could. I have captured none. Probes wait on a behavioural effect that survives. Four redesigns stopped at their own preregistered gates. The stream is known for sceptical, fast empirical iteration. [CONFIRM: name what you have actually read from the stream that shows you this] I want someone who pushes harder than I do. My prior work is verification: proving agent workflows safe before execution, and modelling confabulation-like failures in LLM memory systems. Both ask whether internal state tracks the world.
